claim.pdf_says: D.6.3   Accessing data and files / D.6.3.1   General / D.6.3.2   Names / D.6.3.3   Items overview / D.6.3.4   Item types / D.6.3.4.1   Working-storage records
claim.markdown_says: ## D.6.3 Accessing data and files / ### D.6.3.1 General / ### D.6.3.2 Names / ## D.6.3.3 Items overview / ## D.6.3.4 Item types / ### D.6.3.4.1 Working-storage records
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown heading level does not track the printed numbering depth, so the outline nests wrongly: D.6.3.3 and D.6.3.4 are emitted at '##', making them siblings of their own parent D.6.3 and of the peer subsections D.6.3.1/D.6.3.2 that are emitted at '###'. The same inversion recurs on every page of this batch (1079: D.6.3.5, D.6.3.6; 1081: D.6.4.4, D.6.5.1-D.6.5.3; 1082: D.6.5.3.1-D.6.5.3.3; 1083: D.6.5.4; 1084: D.6.5.5, D.6.5.6; 1085: D.6.5.6.3; 1086: D.6.5.6.4-D.6.5.6.6; 1087: D.6.5.6.7, D.6.5.6.8, D.6.5.7; 1088: D.6.5.8, D.6.6; 1089: D.7). NO TEXT IS LOST - the clause number in the heading text still encodes the true level - so this is an outline/navigation defect, not a normative one. It is also not specific to these pages: across Annex D a depth-4 number is rendered variously as '##' (26x), '###' (23x) and '####' (2x). Fix with one document-wide pass; do not hand-edit only these twelve pages or the inconsistency simply moves.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds.

(1) The kind label is factually false: nothing is missing. PDF page 1078 (printed folio 1048) prints exactly seven headings - D.6.3.3 Items overview, D.6.3.4 Item types, D.6.3.4.1 Working-storage records, D.6.3.4.2 File connectors, D.6.3.4.3 Record areas for files, D.6.3.4.4 Screen records, D.6.3.4.5 Other items. All seven are present in page-1078.md with verbatim text, correct clause numbers, and correct order (lines 7, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, 37). Zero headings, and zero words of body text, are absent.

(2) The claim misquotes the PDF page it names. Three of the six headings it attributes to page 1078 - D.6.3 Accessing data and files, D.6.3.1 General, D.6.3.2 Names - do not appear on page 1078 at all. I rendered page 1077 (printed folio 1047) and they print there. Conversely the claim omits D.6.3.4.2 through D.6.3.4.5, which do print on 1078. The claimed 'inversion' (a '##' next to a sibling '###') is therefore not even observable on page 1078: the on-page markdown is internally self-consistent there, mapping every depth-4 number to '##' and every depth-5 number to '###'.

(3) There is no PDF-side signal for the markdown to have lost. I extracted the span font metadata for both pages with PyMuPDF. Page 1077 and page 1078 each carry exactly one heading typeface at one size: Cambria,Bold at 11.67pt (page 1077: 4 bold spans = running head + D.6.3 + D.6.3.1 + D.6.3.2; page 1078: 8 bold spans = running head + the seven D.6.3.3/D.6.3.4/D.6.3.4.1-.5 headings). Body text is Cambria 10.7pt. So the printed document sets a depth-3 clause (D.6.3), a depth-4 clause (D.6.3.3) and a depth-5 clause (D.6.3.4.1) in the IDENTICAL font at the IDENTICAL point size. The PDF encodes hierarchy solely in the dotted clause number, and the transcription reproduces every clause number exactly. Nothing present in the source is absent from the transcription; the markdown '#' count is a rendering convention the PDF does not specify.

(4) It fails the stated rejection tests. The claim itself concedes 'NO TEXT IS LOST' and 'an outline/navigation defect, not a normative one'. A '##' vs '###' prefix is formatting; it changes no meaning, no normative content, and no COBOL semantics. Under the instruction to reject differences that are only formatting or that do not change meaning, this is not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy.

One sub-assertion of the claim does check out, and it is worth recording separately: the transcription-internal heading-level mapping is inconsistent across Annex D. Tallying numbering depth against '#' count over all Annex D headings gives D.x.y.z.w (the claim's 'depth-4') as '##' 26x, '###' 23x, '####' 2x - matching the claim's figures exactly - and the shallower depths are equally scattered (D.x: 30x '##' / 2x '###'; D.x.y: 61/24/2; D.x.y.z: 79/48/8). That is a genuine cosmetic defect in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, but it is a self-consistency issue in the markdown, not a divergence from the PDF, and it is neither 'missing' nor 'structural' with respect to the canonical source.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF/markdown discrepancy. Every heading printed on page 1078 (D.6.3.3, D.6.3.4, D.6.3.4.1 through D.6.3.4.5) is present in the markdown with verbatim text and correct clause numbers; no text is lost. The claim additionally misattributes D.6.3, D.6.3.1 and D.6.3.2 to page 1078 - those print on page 1077 - and omits D.6.3.4.2-.5 which do print on 1078. Font extraction shows the PDF sets every heading on both pages in one typeface at one size (Cambria,Bold 11.67pt) regardless of clause depth, so the source carries no heading-level information beyond the dotted number the markdown already preserves. What is real, and should be re-filed as a separate cosmetic/consistency item scoped document-wide rather than per-page, is that specs/ISO_COBOL.md maps numbering depth to '#' count inconsistently throughout Annex D (e.g. D.x.y.z.w appears as '##' 26x, '###' 23x, '####' 2x). Severity for that item is cosmetic/navigational, not structural.
